notes: Lines of Sight — an interactive editorial atlas of the Chappe optical telegraph (1791–1855). Single static site, vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no frameworks or network calls; ~5,000 words of original editorial prose across ten plates, with every historical claim cited on the Sources plate and every invented element (vignettes, letter-to-pose teaching table, 1–98 pose numbering, schematic map routes, modelled lengths, symbolic fraud codes) explicitly labelled. Six interactive instruments built from scratch: a scrub-and-play network atlas (SVG map of 26 documented lines plus a Mediterranean inset with year-gated construction and closure), an annotated station plate with 8 hotspots, an explorer for all 98 semaphore poses, a Paris–Lille encoder with animated relay simulation and a true-pace (20 s/symbol) mode, a two-transcript reconstruction of the 1834 Blanc brothers fraud, and a six-question exam with explanations; plus a glossary whose 16 inline dotted terms open popovers. All artwork (tower renderer, engraved France map, hero ridgeline scene) is procedural SVG from one shared generator; Fraunces/EB Garamond/IBM Plex Mono are self-hosted OFL woff2 subsets in assets/fonts. Tested in a Chromium-class browser at 1600px and 390px: timeline scrubbed to peak and selected lines, encoder run at both paces, fraud replayed on/off, exam answered, poses browsed, glossary popovers and contents overlay opened, horizontal overflow checked at phone width (none). No console capture was available in the automation harness, so a clean console is inferred from full DOM construction and zero error-path triggers across all exercised flows rather than from a direct console read; localStorage is not used, so storage guards were not needed. Known limitation: keyboard-shortcut help lists J/K/C/? which were verified via dispatched DOM key events; the harness's synthetic key path could not be exercised end-to-end.
